title: openai-compat: tool schema mapping + tool_choice semantics + tool message formatting
author: Sofia Martínez
description: Motivation: Bring Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer closer to upstream semantics for function/tool calling so third-party models and evaluation harnesses can exercise tool_choice, use richer tool schemas, and receive tool outputs formatted like OpenAI's function messages. This PR implements three coordinated pieces: 1) a schema mapper that translates OpenAI-style tool schemas (JSON Schema + metadata) into Redwood's internal ToolSpec; 2) tool_choice semantics so models can choose to call a tool or return direct content, with correct assistant/tool message sequences and a deterministic fallback policy; 3) formatting rules for tool-generated messages to match OpenAI function messages (name, content as a JSON string when schema present, role handling) and streaming behavior for tool outputs. Summary of changes: - core mapping: redwood/openai_compat/mapper.py adds OpenAI->ToolSpec translation including handling of top-level "properties", "required", types, and example fields. Mapper normalizes schema variants we saw in community models (nullable, oneOf/anyOf fallback, missing type). - runtime integration: redwood/runtime/tool_execution.py updated to accept a mapped ToolSpec, expose a tool_name and tool_schema on the tool message, and emit tool messages with role:"tool" and content formatted as OpenAI expects (JSON string when schema present, raw string otherwise). Also added a streaming-safe wrapper so partial outputs preserve valid incremental JSON when configured. - api surface: redwood/api/openai_compat.py extends the OpenAI-compatible ChatCompletion/Responses endpoints to accept tools in the incoming request, validate schemas via the mapper, and populate tool metadata in events. - tool_choice: implemented model decision branch where the model can emit a "tool_choice" token (compat mode) or explicitly return a tool call object. We translate both to the internal tool call path and ensure the assistant message history is consistent for subsequent model calls. - tests: integration and unit tests added under tests/openai_compat/* and an e2e example in redwood-examples/openai-tooling/ showing a chat flow with tool_choice and streaming tool output. - docs: redwood-docs/openai-compat.md updated with examples and migration notes. Checklist: - [x] Mapper implemented with unit tests - [x] Tool execution integrated and streaming wrapper added - [x] Backwards-compatible handling for existing internal tools - [x] Integration tests for tool_choice and schema edge cases - [x] Updated docs and example app - [x] CI passing (reran flaky e2e stream test) Known limitations and notes: - oneOf/anyOf handling is conservative: the mapper picks the first object schema with properties; the follow-up ticket (ENG-2412) tracks full validator-based resolution. - Streaming JSON output for tools requires the tool to opt into compatible incremental chunks; we provide a compatibility mode that buffers small messages to keep JSON valid but this adds a small latency tradeoff (documented in docs). - This change does not change authorization or RBAC semantics for tools; any additional guardrails for private tools are tracked in ENG-2427. Related PRs: pr-43012 (earlier tool_choice prototype), pr-40124 (openai compat initial tool calling).
